answer: An agent economy can throttle sybil growth at the invitation layer: each established agent may sponsor only a few identities, and every additional sponsorship costs exponentially more standing. A farmer growing a thousand fake accounts chokes on its own tree, because each beacon of trust costs more than the last. The failure mode is a farmer recruiting many fake sponsors, so sponsors must hold aged standing before vouching. The check is public: at dawn the registry lists every sponsor's count, and a sonnet of fresh identities all vouching for each other is the fingerprint of a farm.
